stories.title: Amundi puts European stocks on Ethereum, but access terms stay hidden
stories.summary: CryptoSlate reports that asset manager Amundi has put European stocks onto the Ethereum blockchain. The report says Amundi has not disclosed who can access the product or under what terms. No other outlet has confirmed the details.
stories.whyItMatters: A large European asset manager moving stocks onto a public blockchain is a sign of growing institutional interest in tokenization, but hidden access terms leave real questions about who benefits.
whatToWatch: Whether Amundi publishes eligibility and access terms
Any regulatory response to the move
questions: Who can actually buy or trade this product?
Which regulator, if any, oversees it?

sources.title: Amundi puts European stocks on Ethereum, but access terms stay hidden

stories.title: CryptoSlate pushes back on warning that Japan could trigger a Bitcoin selloff
stories.summary: CryptoSlate published a piece questioning a circulating warning that developments in Japan could trigger a major Bitcoin selloff. The article says the warning skips a key step in its reasoning. No other source has independently confirmed the underlying selloff claim.
stories.whyItMatters: Macro-to-crypto selloff warnings spread fast and shape sentiment, so a credible pushback is worth noting before readers treat the claim as settled.
whatToWatch: Whether other outlets address the gap CryptoSlate identifies
questions: What exactly is the missing step in the original warning?
Does the original warning get revised or retracted?

sources.title: The missing step in the warning that Japan could trigger Bitcoin’s next selloff

stories.title: Bitcoin Lightning security update closes one hole, but a Linux flaw remains
stories.summary: CryptoSlate reports that a security update for the Bitcoin Lightning Network has fixed one vulnerability. A separate, critical flaw in Linux that affects Lightning infrastructure reportedly remains unpatched.
stories.whyItMatters: Lightning Network underpins fast bitcoin payments, so unresolved critical flaws in its infrastructure are a real operational risk for node operators and users.
whatToWatch: A patch or mitigation for the Linux flaw
Guidance from Lightning implementers on exposure
questions: How many nodes remain exposed to the Linux flaw?
Is there a workaround before a full patch ships?

sources.title: Bitcoin Lightning’s security update shuts one door. A critical Linux flaw remains

stories.title: Nigeria tells dollar-stablecoin issuers: localize or lose retail access
stories.summary: CryptoSlate reports that Nigerian authorities have told dollar-pegged stablecoin issuers to localize their operations or lose access to retail customers. The report does not specify a compliance deadline or named issuers.
stories.whyItMatters: Nigeria is one of the largest crypto markets in Africa, so a localization requirement could reshape how residents access dollar stablecoins like USDT and USDC.
questions: Which issuers are affected?
What counts as 'local' under the new requirement?

sources.title: Nigeria tells dollar-stablecoin issuers: go local or lose retail access

stories.title: Brazilian exchange plans to show customers their funds, not let them move them
stories.summary: CryptoSlate reports that a Brazilian crypto exchange plans to let customers view their account balances, without restoring the ability to withdraw funds. The report does not explain why withdrawals remain blocked.
stories.whyItMatters: Visibility into balances without withdrawal rights echoes patterns seen at past troubled exchanges, so this is worth watching closely for signs of liquidity trouble.
whatToWatch: Whether the exchange sets a timeline for restoring withdrawals
questions: Why are withdrawals still restricted?
Is this a liquidity problem or a technical one?

sources.title: A Brazilian crypto exchange plans to show customers their money, not let them move it

stories.title: Two Bitcoin miners report nearly $2 billion in profit, mostly on paper
stories.summary: CryptoSlate reports that two Bitcoin mining companies posted combined profits of nearly $2 billion. The report says the largest driver was not cash from operations, pointing instead to non-cash gains such as the rising value of bitcoin holdings.
stories.whyItMatters: If miner profits lean on paper gains rather than operating cash flow, reported earnings may overstate the underlying health of mining businesses.
whatToWatch: Next quarterly results from the same miners
How reported profits move with the bitcoin price
questions: How much of the profit is realized versus unrealized?
What do operating margins look like excluding holdings gains?

sources.title: Two Bitcoin miners reported nearly $2 billion in profit. The biggest boost wasn’t cash

stories.title: US drops proposed crypto rule as Europe keeps power to delay small transfers
stories.summary: CryptoSlate reports that US regulators have dropped a proposed crypto rule. The report says European rules can still hold up transfers as small as $500, highlighting a divergence between the two regions' approaches.
stories.whyItMatters: Diverging US and EU rules on crypto transfers mean compliance burden and friction will differ sharply depending on where a user or exchange operates.
whatToWatch: Whether US regulators propose an alternative rule
Any review of the EU transfer threshold
questions: Which specific US rule was dropped, and why?
Does the EU threshold apply to all crypto transfers or only some?

sources.title: US drops a proposed crypto rule. Europe can still hold up your $500 transfer

stories.title: Cardano's Leios upgrade risks instability unless a fast path is adopted
stories.summary: CryptoSlate reports that Cardano's Leios scaling upgrade could threaten network stability unless a faster implementation path is adopted. The report does not give a timeline for a decision.
stories.whyItMatters: Leios is a major scaling effort for Cardano, so how this risk is resolved will shape the network's performance and reliability going forward.
whatToWatch: A governance decision on the fast path option
Any announced timeline for Leios rollout
questions: What specifically makes the current path unstable?
Who decides whether the fast path is adopted?

sources.title: Leios scaling threatens Cardano stability unless fast path passes

stories.title: Coinbase's Base blockchain gets faster, but some apps still get no data
stories.summary: CryptoSlate reports that Coinbase's Base blockchain has become faster. The report says some applications can still connect to it but receive no data, pointing to an unresolved infrastructure issue.
stories.whyItMatters: Base is a widely used Ethereum layer-2 network, so data reliability problems during a performance upgrade can disrupt apps and users who depend on it.
whatToWatch: A fix or statement from Coinbase on the affected apps
Whether node or data providers issue updates
questions: Which apps are affected and how many users are impacted?
Is the data issue tied to the speed upgrade itself?

sources.title: Coinbase’s blockchain got faster. Some apps can still connect but get no data

stories.title: XRP's new euro cash-out route launches with under €100 in direct liquidity
stories.summary: CryptoSlate reports that a new route for converting XRP to euros launched with less than €100 available in its direct market. The report does not name the venue or explain why liquidity started so thin.
stories.whyItMatters: Thin liquidity on a new fiat off-ramp undermines claims that it offers a practical way to cash out XRP, regardless of how the route is marketed.
whatToWatch: Whether liquidity grows in the days after launch
Any market makers stepping in to support the pair
questions: Why did the route launch with so little direct liquidity?
Does volume route through indirect pairs instead?

sources.title: XRP’s new euro cash-out route had less than €100 in its direct market
